text:
Jake Oettinger faced 2.6 goals' worth of chances and let none of them in, and that is the gap between what CHI did and what the scoreboard shows. Jordan Greenway had a 48% look in the third period, the best chance of the night, and Oettinger stopped it. CHI out-chanced DAL at even strength, 2.10 expected goals to 1.89, and still lost 4-0.

The game turned in the second period, when DAL out-chanced CHI 1.56 to 0.30 in expected goals. Jason Robertson scored on the power play at 4:58, set up by Mikko Rantanen and Thomas Harley, and Arttu Hyry made it 2-0 at 14:10. Hyry added a backhand at 1:27 of the third on a 5% chance, the least likely goal of the game. Roope Hintz finished it at 9:40, with Tyler Seguin and Robertson assisting. Spencer Knight allowed four on 32 shots, about what DAL's chances deserved (3.44 expected goals against).

CHI pushed hard late, taking 1.45 expected goals to DAL's 0.55 in the third, but had nothing to show for it. The replay math favors DAL, 64% to 36%, so the win was fair even if the margin flattered them. Robertson led the way with a goal, an assist and seven shots on goal. Hyry, the first star, scored twice in 12:00 of ice time. DAL won 37 of 55 faceoffs and went 1 for 4 on the power play, while CHI went 0 for 4.
